 Luka Dončić (back) is out for Sunday’s game against the Pistons. 
 Dončić will miss his second game of the season, the first being an October 28 win over the Clippers. Austin Reaves took on primary playmaking in that game and struggled, shooting 6-of-16 from the field and committing eight turnovers. As for the starting lineup, Quentin Grimes could replace Dončić.

 Austin Reaves, Quentin Grimes, Matisse Thybulle, Jake LaRavia and Walker Kessler will start Sunday’s game against the Pistons. 
 The Lakers won’t have Luka Dončić on Sunday, as he’s out with lower back spasms. Grimes will replace him in the lineup, and he started for the MVP candidate in an October 28 win over the Clippers. Dončić’s absence also means that the Lakers will look to Reaves to initiate even more offense. 
 Luka Dončić 
 LAL 
 Forward-Guard 
 #77 
 Luka Dončić (back) is questionable for Sunday’s game against the Pistons. 
 Dončić, who most recently scored 53 points in Friday’s win over the Trail Blazers, has been on an absolute tear over the last two weeks. If he can’t play on Sunday, Austin Reaves’ role would grow in importance, while Quentin Grimes and Collin Sexton would likely see their minutes increase. 
 Austin Reaves 
 LAL 
 Guard 
 #15 
 Austin Reaves tallied 25 points (8-of-22 FGs, 8-of-8 FTs), three rebounds, two assists, four steals and one three-pointer in Friday’s win over the Trail Blazers. 
 Reaves struggled to begin Friday’s game, missing his first seven shots. However, he shone in the second and fourth quarters, shooting 7-of-12 from the field and scoring 23 of his 25 points. Even with Friday’s poor shooting, Reaves is shooting nearly 51 percent from the field. His fantasy value hasn’t aligned with his top-25 ADP, but Reaves has been a top-50 player through the Lakers’ first 10 games. 
 Luka Dončić 
 LAL 
 Forward-Guard 
 #77 
 Luka Dončić went off in Friday’s win over the Trail Blazers, finishing with 53 points (17-of-33 FGs, 14-of-18 FTs), five rebounds, five assists, one steal and five three-pointers. 
 Dončić finished Friday’s victory with his 11th 50-point game, moving past Kareem Abdul-Jabbar and Allen Iverson to land in tenth on the league’s all-time list. But that wasn’t the only history the Lakers star made on Friday. Dončić has tallied at least 35 points, five rebounds, and five assists in seven straight games, tying Oscar Robertson for the longest such streak in league history. Also, Dončić, who outscored Portland 20-15 in the third quarter, has scored at least 40 points in four straight games. He’s on an incredible run, which is great for those rostering Dončić. 
 Luka Dončić 
 LAL 
 Forward-Guard 
 #77 
 Luka Dončić had himself a night with 40 points (11-of-23 FGs, 12-of-13 FTs), nine rebounds, seven assists, a steal, a block, six 3-pointers, and six turnovers in 116-103 win over the Kings. 
 Luka’s MVP campaign continues in Sacramento where he puts another massive statement game against the Kings. He took over in the third quarter, and the Lakers separated themselves against the Kings in this game. He’s been everything you could’ve wanted and more this season and the hope is that he doesn’t get hurt. 
 Austin Reaves 
 LAL 
 Guard 
 #15 
 Austin Reaves put up 21 points (7-of-15 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), three rebounds, four assists, and a three in win over the Kings. 
 Austin has been one of the most consistent players in the league this season. He does his job as the secondary option in the offense, he hits threes, he gets some assists and plays good defense. The rebounds have been lower than what you would want since he’s been averaging 4 rebounds a game for the past three seasons, and he’s at three this year, but it’s hard to complain all things considered. 
 Austin Reaves 
 LAL 
 Guard 
 #15 
 Austin Reaves lit up the Heat with 27 points (10-of-15 FGs), two rebounds, five assists, four three-pointers and five turnovers on Monday. 
 The last few games had been rough for Reaves, but he was able to get back on track in this one. The turnovers still weren’t great, and he now has 24 over his last four outings. However, he was far more efficient as a scorer, which helped the Lakers secure a second win in as many days. Reaves has been a high-level second option behind Luka Dončić this season, though the turnovers need to be cleaned up for him to match his production from last year. 
 Luka Dončić 
 LAL 
 Forward-Guard 
 #77 
 Luka Dončić led the Lakers with 42 points (14-of-24 FGs, 8-of-10 FTs), seven rebounds, 13 assists, two steals and six three-pointers in a 138-117 win over the Heat on Monday. 
 It has been an unreal start to the season for Dončić, and Monday’s performance was just another chapter. He has scored at least 35 points and knocked down at least six three-pointers in each of his last five appearances, while going for at least 40 in four of those outings. The one game he didn’t score 40, he had 37, which was also the only game during this stretch where he shot below 50 percent from the floor. Dončić set a new season high for assists in this game as well. He has been an elite offensive engine, and he’ll look to stay hot against the Kings on Wednesday. 
 Austin Reaves 
 LAL 
 Guard 
 #15 
 Austin Reaves tallied 19 points (6-of-16 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), three rebounds, four assists and two three-pointers in Sunday’s win over the Raptors. 
 After committing eight turnovers in Friday’s loss to the Warriors, Reaves committed three against the Raptors. He didn’t shoot the ball particularly well on Sunday, but Reaves entered the game shooting 54.8 percent from the field and 42.4 percent from beyond the arc. He’ll look to bounce back on Monday when the Lakers host the Heat. 
 Luka Dončić 
 LAL 
 Forward-Guard 
 #77 
 Luka Dončić finished Sunday’s win over the Raptors with 45 points (12-of-23 FGs, 13-of-13 FTs), 15 rebounds, six assists, five steals, one block and eight three-pointers. 
 Dončić put on a show Sunday night, shooting high percentages from the field and the foul line as part of an elite stat line. With the Lakers’ deep reserves failing to put the Raptors away, head coach JJ Redick had to insert four starters back into the game. That got Dončić four more points from the foul line. The lone negative was the seven turnovers, but the stat line was so robust that few will complain. The Lakers play four games next week, starting with the Heat on Monday.

 Josh Giddey produced 19 points (7-of-12 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), seven rebounds, 15 assists, one steal and one three-pointer in Sunday’s loss to the 76ers.
 Despite the outcome, this was Giddey’s best performance of the season. Scoring in double figures for the sixth straight game, he recorded season highs in points and assists against the 76ers.  Nic Claxton (hamstring) recorded four points (2-of-3 FGs), four rebounds, four assists and two blocks in Sunday’s loss to the 76ers.
 Injured early in the preseason, Claxton was limited to 16-20 minutes in his Bulls debut on Sunday. He played 18 minutes and recorded a few rebounds, assists and blocks. Claxton came off the bench, with Jalen Smith (17/8/2, four blocks and two three-pointers) remaining in the starting lineup. The roles will reverse eventually, but not until Claxton’s minutes restriction is lifted.

 Caleb Wilson amassed 18 points (7-of-18 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), five rebounds, two steals and two three-pointers in Sunday’s loss to the 76ers.
 This wasn’t Wilson’s most efficient game; he needed 18 shots to score 18 points. However, he has committed three turnovers or fewer in eight straight games, a far cry from the nine he committed in his debut against the Raptors. Despite shooting 40.6 percent from the field, Wilson is providing top-100 fantasy value, which aligns with his preseason ADP.

 Matas Buzelis recorded 19 points (6-of-10 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), five rebounds, two assists, one block and three three-pointers in Sunday’s loss to the 76ers.
 Buzelis has gotten off to a slow start, seemingly struggling to find his place in the Bulls’ offense with Caleb Wilson in the fold. The third-year forward had no such issues on Sunday, shooting 60 percent from the field. Buzelis’ 19 points were his most in a game since October 24, when he scored a season-high 21 against the Wizards. The Bulls play three games next week, starting with the Spurs on Wednesday.

 Joel Embiid finished Sunday’s win over the Bulls with 18 points (7-of-19 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), 10 rebounds, five assists and two steals.
 Coming off one of the worst games of his career, Embiid was far more impactful on Sunday. Eight of the former MVP’s 10 rebounds were on the offensive end, helping Philadelphia extend possessions and outscore Chicago 33-12 in second-chance points. This was Embiid’s third game this season with at least 10 rebounds and five assists, and his first since October 24 against the Bucks.

 After scoring eight points in a poor showing against the Cavaliers on Friday, James benefited from facing one of the NBA’s worst defenses on Sunday. The 41-year-old forward shot well and finished with his second game with at least 20 points, five rebounds and five assists this season. The 76ers play three games next week with no back-to-backs, which should help James get his rest.
